regions.translation:
Tram Construction and Operating Regulations (not applicable)
Railway Construction and Operating Regulations (applicable)
regions.breakdown: BOStrab is an acronym for 'Verordnung über den Bau und Betrieb der Straßenbahnen' (Ordinance on the Construction and Operation of Trams). It is crossed out, indicating its non-applicability here. EBO is an acronym for 'Eisenbahn-Bau- und Betriebsordnung' (Railway Construction and Operating Regulations), indicating its applicability.

where_youd_see_it: You would see this sign near railway tracks or tram lines, especially at points where different regulatory frameworks might apply.
cultural_note: In Germany, 'BOStrab' and 'EBO' are two distinct sets of regulations governing different types of rail transport. BOStrab applies to streetcars (trams), while EBO applies to regular railways. A sign like this indicates which set of rules is legally binding for a specific section of track, often important for safety and operational procedures.
